PURPOSE.what_this_amendment_does: Replaces 'the authority's controls plus executor discipline' (DF-13) with a MACHINE-ENFORCED read boundary, and closes the measured defects the arming-package certification reported, without redesigning the authority or widening any read.
what_it_does_not_do: Does not add a read, widen a read's scope, or add a PACMI operation.
Does not execute any read or any PACMI call.
Does not arm the grant, and withdraws ARMED=true as a standing claim (see ARMED_STATE).
Does not edit v1.0.0 through v1.0.3, the RC-9a record, or either arming determination.

EXECUTOR_BOUNDARY.rule: NORMATIVE. Every governed read (V-R1..V-R4, G-R1..G-R4, X-R1) and every PACMI operation MUST be performed through the safe-read executor in scripts/infra-read/ and in no other way. Invoking gh, vercel or git directly for any of them is outside this authority and is refused under RC-10.

implementation.registry: scripts/infra-read/ops.ts — the CLOSED operation registry: every op's tool, fixed path pattern or fixed argv, freshness class, node ids and concrete field allowlist.
implementation.guards: scripts/infra-read/guards.ts — invocation construction, EXACT-SHAPE validation, and in-process projection.
implementation.xcc1: scripts/infra-read/xcc1.ts — the credential-free git environment and its runtime preflight.
implementation.executor: scripts/infra-read/executor.ts — ordering, RC-9b, scope, RNA-1, freshness, post-projection conformance and detector re-check, validated evidence records.
implementation.protocol: scripts/infra-read/protocol.ts — the terminating RC-9a -> DN-0 -> reads -> evidence protocol.
implementation.entry: scripts/infra-read/run-governed-reads.ts — refuses unless --execute, --certified-candidate and --out are all supplied.

EXECUTOR_BOUNDARY.not_a_passthrough: A caller names an op id and passes typed parameters. It never supplies an endpoint, a method, a flag, an argv or an environment. Parameters are validated against closed regexes (team_*, prj_*, 40-hex SHA, numeric ruleset id, governed branch names) and the built path is re-checked against the op's anchored pattern.
EXECUTOR_BOUNDARY.allowlist_not_denylist: The operative control is an ALLOWLIST comparison: the built argv must equal, token for token, the ONE shape its op permits. Denylists exist only to give precise refusal tokens. Measured by mutation M02: emptying the gh denylist did NOT let `--show-token` through; it was still refused by the exact-shape check, under a different token.

tool_pinning.rule: The flag semantics were measured against these versions. Any other version fails closed with STOP_TOOL_VERSION_DRIFT.

EXECUTOR_BOUNDARY.process_model: Every child is spawned with an argument array and shell:false. The Vercel CLI is run as `node <APPDATA>/npm/node_modules/vercel/dist/vc.js ...`, never through the .cmd shim, so no shell ever concatenates arguments.

explicitly_refused_measured_on_gh_2.93.0: -X / --method other than the literal GET form, including --method=VALUE
absence of --method (gh's GET default is not relied on)
GITHUB_METHOD_GUARD.environment: GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GH_HOST, GH_DEBUG and DEBUG are removed, so the credential used is the keyring credential RC-9a characterizes. GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1, GH_PAGER='', NO_COLOR=1.

VERCEL_METHOD_GUARD.measured_semantics_that_differ_from_gh: In the installed Vercel CLI 54.14.2 bundle, `--method GET` combined with -f/-F sends the fields as a JSON BODY on a GET; it does NOT build a query string. The gh idiom `-X GET -f key=value` therefore cannot be used to express query parameters. All query parameters are encoded LITERALLY in the registry path.
explicitly_refused_measured_on_vercel_ap: -X and any --method other than the literal GET form
--generate (e.g. --generate=curl emits a request that carries the token)
VERCEL_METHOD_GUARD.operation_ids_refused: The endpoint must begin with '/' and match the op's anchored pattern. A provider operation identifier (e.g. deleteProject) can never be passed as the endpoint: STOP_VERCEL_WRITE_OPERATION_ID.
VERCEL_METHOD_GUARD.decrypt: decrypt=false is part of V-R2.L5's literal pattern; decrypt=true cannot match any pattern in the registry.
VERCEL_METHOD_GUARD.environment: VERCEL_TOKEN, VERCEL_ORG_ID, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID and DEBUG are removed.

OUTPUT_PROJECTION.rule: Provider output is parsed in-process and reduced to the op's CONCRETE field allowlist. Unknown fields are dropped silently and never echoed. The raw object goes out of scope inside the executor and is never logged, written or serialized.
three_layers: 1. project(): only allowlisted leaves survive; presence-only fields (passwordProtection, trustedIps) become booleans.

2. assertProjectionConforms(): every leaf of what is about to become evidence must match the allowlist. This is what refuses a projector that was bypassed or mutated into passing the raw object (mutation M04, M17).
3. the supplemental detectors re-scan the projection; a secret-shaped value in an ALLOWLISTED field (e.g. a deploy-hook URL placed in a name) is still refused (mutation M09).
OUTPUT_PROJECTION.validated_records_only: Only records produced by the executor are marked validated; the entry point refuses to write anything else (STOP_UNVALIDATED_EVIDENCE).

allowlist_concretization.V-R3: v1.0.0 defined V-R3's allowlist by SUBTRACTION ('the whole Git integration block minus the prohibitions'), the one place RC-5's positive-allowlist rule did not hold. It is replaced by a concrete enumeration in ops.ts. Keys absent at read time are recorded as absent under RC-12, never read as absent features.
allowlist_concretization.V-R1_autodeploy_locus: LOCUS PIN, NOT SCOPE WIDENING. v1.0.0's V-R1 made the automatic-deployment limb MANDATORY but pinned no field. gitProviderOptions.createDeployments is the field a prior measurement of this project record found carrying that semantic content (2026-09-21, 'enabled'). It is added to V-R1's concrete allowlist as the locus of an obligation v1.0.0 already imposed. It remains RECALLED for the executing lane under RC-8: if absent, DN-1's limb is STOP_AUTODEPLOY_POSTURE_UNEXPOSED, not 'disabled'.
allowlist_concretization.G-R2_witness: G-R2.WITNESS reads the branch object (name, protected, commit.sha) for the SAME encoded path as limbs A and C. A 404 on protection is interpreted only if the witness resolved, so a mis-encoded branch name cannot be read as 'unprotected' (DF-3/DF-5 class).

SUPPLEMENTAL_SECRET_SCAN.rule: ADDITIVE. pnpm secrets:scan is unchanged and still runs. Its green is NOT evidence of absence for the classes below, which it has no detector for.
detectors: AUTHORIZATION_HEADER (including GitHub's own 'Authorization: token <x>' form, a gap found by this lane's own test)
OPAQUE_HIGH_ENTROPY (>=40 chars, mixed case and digits; pure lowercase hex SHAs excluded)
applied_at: every projection, inside the executor, before a record exists
every evidence file the entry point writes, before it reports success
SUPPLEMENTAL_SECRET_SCAN.non_echo: Findings report detector id and offset only, never the matched text.
SUPPLEMENTAL_SECRET_SCAN.empty_set_is_failure: Scanning zero files is STOP_EVIDENCE_SCAN_EMPTY_SET, not a pass.
SUPPLEMENTAL_SECRET_SCAN.not_done_deliberately: Exact-match comparison against the live credential values. That would require reading the token into the scanning process, which DF11 forbids.

FRESHNESS_CLASSIFICATION.rule: Not every authorized read belongs in the read-only phase. A current observation is evidence for its instant; it never permanently satisfies a future pre-mutation node.
FRESHNESS_CLASSIFICATION.V-R4_reason: DN-11's verification is a THROUGHOUT clause around M-7: a pre-act and a post-act reading bracketing the mutation. A reading taken in a read-only phase brackets nothing. The executor refuses V-R4 in READ_ONLY_CONTROL_PLANE_PHASE (STOP_FRESHNESS_CLASS_NOT_EXECUTABLE_IN_THIS_PHASE).
consumers_that_must_re_read_immediately: DN-14 (M-6): V-R3 re-captured immediately before the act; a read-phase V-R3 is DN-3 evidence, not M-6's prestate.
DN-7 (M-8): X-R1 (source head and release-ref absence), G-R2 limb D and V-R3's release-reference limb, immediately before the create.
DN-8/DN-9/DN-10 (M-3/M-1/M-9): G-R2 on the target ref, immediately before the protection act.
DN-12 (M-2): G-R3 then G-R2 on the measured default branch, immediately before the act.
DN-11 (M-7): V-R1, V-R4 (bracketing), G-R2 and G-R3, immediately around the act.

RC9B_ORDER.rule: RESTORED. G-R1 MUST precede G-R2, and G-R1 precedes every other G-R* read (TI-14 binds every later GitHub read to the repository identity G-R1 establishes).
RC9B_ORDER.why_it_was_lost: RC-9's original text put the G-R1 permission object BEFORE the first read. The v1.0.2 split moved that capture into the first G-R1 read (RC-9b) to remove a circularity, and in doing so dropped the ordering it implied.
RC9B_ORDER.discharge: RC-9b is discharged DURING G-R1: the projection must contain the permissions object with at least one boolean. If it does not, G-R2 is refused.
RC9B_ORDER.mechanical_enforcement: STOP_GR1_NOT_FIRST for any G-R* before G-R1; STOP_RC9B_NOT_DISCHARGED for any G-R2 op without a successful G-R1 that captured the permission object in the SAME executor context.

supersedes.why_moved: A normative command contract lived only in an evidence record. It is moved into the authority here, and the evidence record is left unedited.
supersedes.parent_rule_verbatim: X-R1 MUST be invoked with git credential helpers reset and terminal prompting disabled. The mandated form is: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -c credential.helper= ls-remote <origin-url>
supersedes.parent_guarantee_verbatim: With the helper list reset to empty AND terminal prompting disabled, git has no mechanism by which to obtain or present a credential for an HTTPS remote. It cannot silently authenticate.
supersedes.classification_of_the_parent_guarantee: FALSE IN GENERAL. Measured on this host: core.askPass, GIT_ASKPASS and SSH_ASKPASS each return a password with that exact form. It held on this host only because none of the three was set, which is an environmental fact, not a property of the command.

PACMI_REFRESH_DISPOSITION.consequence_for_rc9a: Execution-time RC-9a records the CURRENT credential state at its instant. A historical expiry is never reused.

EXPIRY_READ_WITHDRAWN.finding_addressed: AP-NB-EXPIRY-OUTSIDE-PACMI: the Vercel expiry was read from auth.json, a file read outside the provider-native PACMI set, from a file that also holds the token.
EXPIRY_READ_WITHDRAWN.rule: The executor does not read auth.json or any credential store. Vercel credential validity is established provider-natively by PACMI-V1 succeeding at the RC-9a instant, which immediately precedes the reads.
EXPIRY_READ_WITHDRAWN.what_is_lost: The absolute expiry timestamp. It is not needed: the protocol runs RC-9a, DN-0 and the reads back to back, and a credential that expires mid-run produces visible provider errors, not silent success.

ARMED_STATE.rule: ARMED=true is WITHDRAWN AS A STANDING CLAIM. It was a correct determination at its instant (docs/ops/release/CV1_INFRA_CONTROL_PLANE_READ_ARMING_DETERMINATION_v1.0.1.json), bound to eleven blobs, one session and a Vercel horizon that has since passed. This delta changes the effective package.
ARMED_STATE.how_arming_now_happens: At RUNTIME, by the executor, on every execution: runtime RC-9a (LIMB_3) -> DN-0 as the last pre-read act (LIMB_2, including verification that the three certification events exist and carry passing VERDICT.verdict values — LIMB_1) -> AC-1 evaluated -> reads. No further conceptual arming authority is needed or created.
certification_events_required_at_runtime: docs/ops/release/CV1_INFRA_EXECUTOR_HARDENING_IC_v1.0.0.json (to be materialized from the bounded IC of THIS delta, with VERDICT.verdict matching ^INFRA_EXECUTOR_HARDENING_IC_PASS(_WITH_NONBLOCKING_FINDINGS)?$)

sequence: 1. The candidate is committed and independently certified.
2. Runtime RC-9a: PACMI-G1, PACMI-V1, PACMI-V2, PACMI-V3 and the XCC-1 preflight — current credential state, all three planes.
3. DN-0 against the execution HEAD, as the LAST pre-read act.
4. NO COMMIT. Before EVERY read the executor re-checks that HEAD equals the DN-0 HEAD and the worktree is clean.

5. The governed reads, in the fixed order G-R1, G-R3, G-R2 (witness/A/C per governed ref, then rulesets), G-R4, V-R2 scopes, inventories and named target, V-R1, V-R3, V-R2 role limbs (other projects only), XCC-1 preflight, X-R1.
6. Only afterward, the evidence is committed, as ADDITIONS only, with parent == the DN-0 HEAD, verified by assertEvidenceCommitParent.
TERMINATING_DN0_PROTOCOL.why_it_terminates: DN-0 evidence is part of the post-read evidence commit. Nothing is committed between DN-0 and the reads, so the HEAD DN-0 measured is the HEAD the reads ran against. Committing DN-0 first would move HEAD, and a DN-0 'satisfied at this head and nowhere else' would have to be re-run forever.
TERMINATING_DN0_PROTOCOL.post_certification_additions: DN-0 accepts the certified candidate as an ancestor of HEAD only if every change since it is an ADDITION of a certification-event file (docs/ops/release/CV1_INFRA_*_IC_v*.json). Materializing this delta's own IC therefore does not invalidate the certification it records; any modification does.
